\[
xyz = 3,
\]
\[
(x-y)(y-z)(z-x) = 4,
\]
\[
(x+y)(y+z)(z+x) = 40.
\]

Compute the minimum possible value for \( x \).

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

\[
\boxed{\sqrt[3]{\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}}}
\]

A proof of minimality:

By cyclic symmetry, the minimum attainable \(x\) occurs when \(x\) is the smallest of the three variables, so assume
\[
x<y<z.
\]
Let
\[
m=\frac yx>1,\qquad n=\frac zx>1,\qquad p=mn,\qquad s=m+n.
\]
From \(xyz=3\),
\[
x^3=\frac3p.
\]

The other two equations become
\[
(m+1)(m+n)(n+1)=\frac{40mn}{3}
\]
and
\[
(m-1)(n-m)(n-1)=\frac{4mn}{3}.
\]
Using \(p=mn\) and \(s=m+n\), the first is
\[
s(p+s+1)=\frac{40p}{3}. \tag{1}
\]
Also,
\[
(m-1)(n-1)=p-s+1,\qquad n-m=\sqrt{s^2-4p},
\]
so the second gives
\[
\sqrt{s^2-4p}\,(p-s+1)=\frac{4p}{3}. \tag{2}
\]

Eliminating \(s\) from (1) and (2) yields the polynomial
\[
27p^6-774p^5+6121p^4-11548p^3+6121p^2-774p+27=0.
\]
Dividing by \(p^3\) and setting \(q=p+\frac1p\), this becomes
\[
27q^3-774q^2+6040q-10000=0
\]
\[
=(q-10)\bigl(27q^2-504q+1000\bigr)=0.
\]
Thus
\[
q\in\left\{10,\frac{84+26\sqrt6}{9},\frac{84-26\sqrt6}{9}\right\}.
\]
The largest possible positive \(p\) comes from the largest \(q\), namely
\[
q=\frac{84+26\sqrt6}{9}.
\]
The corresponding larger value of \(p\) is
\[
p=9+3\sqrt6.
\]
Since \(x^3=3/p\), we get
\[
x^3\ge \frac{3}{9+3\sqrt6}
=\frac1{3+\sqrt6}
=\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}.
\]

This bound is attained by
\[
x=\sqrt[3]{\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}},\qquad
y=3x,\qquad
z=(3+\sqrt6)x.
\]
Indeed,
\[
xyz=3,\qquad (x-y)(y-z)(z-x)=4,\qquad (x+y)(y+z)(z+x)=40.
\]

Therefore the minimum possible value of \(x\) is

\[
\boxed{\sqrt[3]{\frac{3-\sqrt6}{3}}}.
\]
